quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Marek repairs old radios in a small workshop behind his house. He collects broken sets from flea markets, replaces the worn parts and polishes the wooden cases until they shine. Collectors now travel from other towns to buy them, and he keeps a waiting list.
options: Some people enjoy fixing things at home.
Marek sells his radios to shops in other towns.
Marek polishes wooden radio cases in his workshop.
Marek restores old radios that collectors want.
quests.correctAnswer: Marek restores old radios that collectors want.
quests.hint: An answer can be true and still too general. Look for one that fits this paragraph and no other.
quests.explanation: The paragraph is about restoring radios and the demand from collectors that results. The 'fixing things' option is too broad, and the polishing option is only one step of the work.
keyPoints: Marek repairs old radios in a workshop behind his house.
He replaces worn parts and polishes the cases.
Collectors travel to buy them, and there is a waiting list.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The town choir began with six singers in a church hall. Neighbours told friends, and within two years sixty people were coming every Wednesday. This year the choir performed at the harbour festival, where hundreds stopped to listen.
options: Music brings communities together in towns everywhere in the world.
A small choir has grown fast and now sings to crowds.
Six singers first met in a church hall.
The harbour festival was created by members of a local choir.
quests.correctAnswer: A small choir has grown fast and now sings to crowds.
quests.hint: Watch for options that could describe almost any choir. Prefer the one built from this paragraph's details.
quests.explanation: The paragraph tracks growth from six singers to sixty and then to a public performance. The first option is too broad, and the second names only the starting point.
keyPoints: The choir started with only six singers.
Word of mouth raised attendance to sixty in two years.
It has now performed for hundreds at the harbour festival.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Anneli's grandmother has kept a garden diary for fifty years. Each entry records the weather, the first flowers of the season and everything she planted. Anneli is now turning the entries into a book, hoping other gardeners will find the notes useful.
options: Fifty years of garden notes are becoming a book.
People like to keep records of their lives for years.
Anneli's grandmother writes about the weather each day.
Anneli's grandmother plans to sell her garden.
quests.correctAnswer: Fifty years of garden notes are becoming a book.
quests.hint: Ask which option keeps the paragraph's key purpose, not just its topic.
quests.explanation: The diary is the topic, but the paragraph's point is that Anneli is turning it into something useful for others. The wrong options are too general, too narrow or unrelated.
keyPoints: Anneli's grandmother has kept a garden diary for fifty years.
It records weather, flowers and plantings.
Anneli is making it into a book for other gardeners.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Jorge's bus was cancelled, so he decided to cycle to his interview across town. He arrived ten minutes early, still a little out of breath, and the interviewer laughed and offered him water. Jorge got the job, and he still tells the story to new colleagues.
options: Buses are far less reliable than bicycles for getting to interviews.
Jorge's interviewer laughed and offered him a glass of water.
Jorge overcame a cancelled bus by cycling to his interview.
Jorge enjoys telling stories about his interview to colleagues.
quests.correctAnswer: Jorge overcame a cancelled bus by cycling to his interview.
quests.hint: Include the problem, the choice and how it ended, if you can.
quests.explanation: The problem was the cancelled bus, Jorge's response was cycling, and the result was a job. The other options pick a detail, a side effect or a broad claim the paragraph never makes.
keyPoints: Jorge's bus was cancelled before his interview.
He cycled across town and arrived early.
He got the job and still tells the story.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Every autumn, the lake near Sana's village fills with thousands of migrating birds. Visitors bring binoculars and sit quietly on the wooden platforms, and local guides explain which species have arrived. The small guesthouses in the village are booked months ahead.
options: Migrating birds bring visitors and business to a village.
Sana's village is famous for its wooden platforms.
Thousands of birds visit lakes in many countries around the world.
Local guides explain to visitors which species have arrived.
quests.correctAnswer: Migrating birds bring visitors and business to a village.
quests.hint: Look for the effect of the birds' arrival, not just the birds.
quests.explanation: The birds attract visitors, and visitors support guides and guesthouses. An option about birds in general is too broad, and one about guides only covers a small part.
keyPoints: Thousands of birds arrive at the lake each autumn.
Visitors watch them from platforms with help from guides.
Local guesthouses are fully booked well in advance.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Ms. Ito's history class used to read the textbook silently. This term she asks students to act out short scenes from the chapters instead. Test results have improved, and students say the events are easier to remember when they have played the people involved.
options: Students enjoy performing on stage more than reading.
Acting out history helps students remember and score better.
Ms. Ito's class reads the textbook silently.
Acting is a better subject than history for most students.
quests.correctAnswer: Acting out history helps students remember and score better.
quests.hint: Compare the old method, the new method and the result.
quests.explanation: The paragraph contrasts silent reading with role-play and reports better results. One wrong option describes the old method and another makes an unsupported comparison of subjects.
keyPoints: Ms. Ito's students used to read the history textbook silently.
They now act out scenes from the chapters.
Results have improved, and events are easier to remember.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: When the river floods, muddy water can enter the basement of the old library. Staff now keep valuable books on high shelves and check the weather forecast each evening. On stormy nights, volunteers wait with pumps and plastic sheets in case the water rises.
options: Heavy storms damage most of the books in this region.
The old library's basement is already filled with river mud.
The library has prepared to protect its books from floods.
Volunteers use pumps to keep the river from flooding.
quests.correctAnswer: The library has prepared to protect its books from floods.
quests.hint: Ask what all these actions have in common.
quests.explanation: Moving books, checking forecasts and waiting with pumps are all ways of protecting the collection. The wrong options describe the flood as already happening, credit the volunteers with stopping the river, or exaggerate the damage.
keyPoints: The old library is at risk when the river floods.
Staff store valuable books on high shelves and watch the forecast.
Volunteers stand ready with pumps on stormy nights.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A new app helps people find free parking spaces. Drivers report an empty spot when they leave, and the app shows nearby spaces to others. Testing in the city centre showed drivers spent about six fewer minutes searching, though the app works best when many people use it.
options: A parking app saves time but needs many users.
The app charges drivers for every space they report.
Six minutes is the longest time anyone searches for parking.
Drivers in the city centre cannot find spaces anywhere.
quests.correctAnswer: A parking app saves time but needs many users.
quests.hint: The final clause often adds a limit. Does your answer include it?
quests.explanation: The paragraph explains the app's benefit and a condition for it to work. The wrong options exaggerate the parking problem, invent charges or misuse a number.
keyPoints: The app shows free parking spaces reported by other drivers.
City-centre tests saved drivers about six minutes.
It works best when many people take part.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The two nurses at the village clinic worked long hours until the district added a third. Waiting times fell, and appointments no longer ran late. The original nurses now have time for home visits, which especially helps older patients who cannot travel.
options: Older patients prefer visits at home to clinic appointments.
The village clinic has now closed its appointment service for good.
The two original nurses now work longer hours.
A third nurse cut waiting times and enabled home visits.
quests.correctAnswer: A third nurse cut waiting times and enabled home visits.
quests.hint: See how one change leads to two separate benefits.
quests.explanation: A third nurse reduced the workload, which shortened waits and freed time for home visits. The wrong options reverse the result or claim a preference not stated.
keyPoints: The village clinic had only two nurses working long hours.
A third nurse was added, and waiting times fell.
The original nurses now make home visits to older patients.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Before she sells a used phone, Fatou resets it, removes her accounts and takes clear photos of the screen and back. She lists every scratch honestly. Buyers trust her, and her phones sell within a day, usually for more than similar ones online.
options: Fatou earns more money than any other phone seller online.
Used phones are usually sold for less than new ones.
Fatou takes clear photos of the screen and back of each phone.
Fatou sells used phones fast by preparing them and being honest.
quests.correctAnswer: Fatou sells used phones fast by preparing them and being honest.
quests.hint: Choose the option that combines her actions with their effect.
quests.explanation: Her careful preparation and honest description build trust, and that explains the quick, better-priced sales. The wrong options exaggerate her success, focus on one action or state a general claim.
keyPoints: Fatou resets and photographs each phone before selling it.
She describes every scratch honestly.
Buyers trust her, so her phones sell fast at good prices.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The tenants in Building C were tired of the lift breaking down every week. They wrote a joint letter, collected forty signatures and delivered it to the landlord's office together. Two weeks later, engineers arrived, and the lift has run smoothly ever since.
options: Engineers replaced every lift in the building last month.
Tenants' joint letter got their broken lift repaired.
Landlords usually ignore complaints from their tenants.
Forty tenants signed a letter addressed to the landlord.
quests.correctAnswer: Tenants' joint letter got their broken lift repaired.
quests.hint: An action is only half a story. Look for the option that also says what it achieved.
quests.explanation: The letter was the tenants' action, and the repaired lift was its result. Stopping at the signatures leaves out whether the action worked.
keyPoints: Tenants in Building C were frustrated by a lift that often broke.
They wrote a joint letter with forty signatures.
Engineers came and the lift now works reliably.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Selin's team spent a month building a small robot for the school science fair. They tested the wheels, rewrote the code twice and painted the body bright yellow. On the day, the robot crossed the maze in under a minute and won second prize.
options: Selin's team built a robot that won second prize.
Selin's team rewrote the robot's code again and again.
Robots are more popular than other science fair projects.
Selin's team painted their robot bright yellow.
quests.correctAnswer: Selin's team built a robot that won second prize.
quests.hint: Notice how much of the paragraph is about preparation, and where it leads.
quests.explanation: The team's effort led to a robot that worked and earned a prize. Options about the paint or the code describe stages along the way but not the outcome.
keyPoints: Selin's team built a robot over a month.
They tested it, improved the code and painted it.
It crossed the maze quickly and won second prize.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Last summer's heatwave dried out the reservoir, and the town had to limit water use. Gardens went brown, car washes closed and families took shorter showers. Officials now plan to build a second reservoir so that a dry summer will not cause the same restrictions.
options: Officials have already finished building a second reservoir.
Gardens turned brown during last summer's long heatwave.
Water shortages have led to plans for a second reservoir.
Car washes are the biggest users of the town's water.
quests.correctAnswer: Water shortages have led to plans for a second reservoir.
quests.hint: Follow the chain from cause to consequence to plan.
quests.explanation: Heat emptied the reservoir, restrictions followed, and officials are now planning a way to prevent a repeat. The wrong options are effects only, invented facts or a plan described as complete.
keyPoints: A heatwave dried out the town's reservoir.
Water use had to be limited, affecting gardens and businesses.
Officials plan a second reservoir to prevent future restrictions.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Whenever Halima skips breakfast, she feels tired by ten o'clock and struggles to follow lessons. When she eats porridge with fruit, she stays alert until lunch. Her teacher suggested she note what she eats and how she feels, and the pattern has become clear.
options: Eating breakfast helps Halima stay alert at school.
Fruit is the only food that keeps students alert.
Halima's teacher makes her eat porridge every morning.
Halima has trouble following lessons at all times.
quests.correctAnswer: Eating breakfast helps Halima stay alert at school.
quests.hint: Two situations are being compared. What does the comparison prove?
quests.explanation: Comparing days with and without breakfast shows the link between eating and alertness. The wrong options invent a rule, ignore the 'when she skips' condition, or exaggerate the role of fruit.
keyPoints: Halima feels tired and distracted when she skips breakfast.
On days she eats porridge with fruit, she stays alert until lunch.
Keeping notes helped her notice the pattern.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The old cinema's roof leaked for years, so the seats got wet and audiences shrank. When the owners finally repaired the roof and replaced the seats, people slowly began to return. The cinema now sells out on Friday nights.
options: The cinema owners closed the building for several years.
Audiences shrank because films became less popular.
Wet seats are the most common reason cinemas close.
Repairs brought the cinema's audience back.
quests.correctAnswer: Repairs brought the cinema's audience back.
quests.hint: Find the cause of the decline and the cause of the recovery.
quests.explanation: The leak made the cinema unpleasant, and fixing it reversed the decline. Wrong options invent a closure, blame a different cause or make a broad claim.
keyPoints: A leaking roof made seats wet and drove audiences away.
The owners repaired the roof and replaced the seats.
People returned, and Friday shows now sell out.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Trains from the airport take twenty-five minutes and cost more, while buses take fifty minutes but are cheap. Trains run every ten minutes; buses run every half hour. Travellers in a hurry usually choose the train, but many students and tourists prefer the bus.
options: The airport is served by both trains and buses.
Travellers in a hurry always choose to take the bus.
Most tourists take the train because it is so cheap.
The airport train is faster, but the bus is cheaper.
quests.correctAnswer: The airport train is faster, but the bus is cheaper.
quests.hint: For a comparison, check that each feature stays attached to the right item.
quests.explanation: The paragraph sets speed and frequency against cost, which explains why different travellers choose differently. Wrong options swap the features or state only the obvious.
keyPoints: Airport trains are quicker and run more often.
Buses take longer but cost much less.
Travellers choose according to their needs.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Living in the countryside gave Oscar quiet, fresh air and a large garden. But the nearest doctor was forty minutes away, and there was no cinema. Since moving to a small city, he has traded some peace for convenience and says he does not miss the mud.
options: Oscar's garden in the city is larger than the one before.
Oscar weighs country peace against city convenience after moving.
The nearest doctor is forty minutes from Oscar's new home.
Oscar has decided to move back to the countryside.
quests.correctAnswer: Oscar weighs country peace against city convenience after moving.
quests.hint: What did Oscar gain, and what did he give up?
quests.explanation: The paragraph balances the benefits of the countryside against its inconveniences and shows Oscar's judgement. The wrong options mix up the two places or reverse his move.
keyPoints: Oscar enjoyed the quiet and space of the countryside.
Services like a doctor and cinema were far away.
He now lives in a small city and prefers the convenience.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: In Priyanka's family, weekends are for cooking together, and dinner takes hours. At her friend Mira's house, meals are quick, and everyone eats when they are hungry. Priyanka enjoys both styles, though she says the long dinners are where her family tells its stories.
options: Priyanka contrasts long family dinners with quick meals.
Priyanka's friend Mira cooks for hours every weekend.
Family stories are told only at long dinners.
Priyanka dislikes eating quickly at other people's houses.
quests.correctAnswer: Priyanka contrasts long family dinners with quick meals.
quests.hint: Sort the details into two groups, then choose the option that compares them.
quests.explanation: Two households have different mealtime habits, and Priyanka values something different in each. Wrong options swap the families, invent dislike or turn 'where' into 'only'.
keyPoints: Priyanka's family cooks together and dinner lasts hours.
Mira's household eats quickly and casually.
Priyanka enjoys both but links long dinners to family stories.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A hearing test is simple and painless. The audiologist places soft headphones on the patient and plays quiet sounds at different pitches. Each time the patient hears a sound, they press a button. The results appear as a chart that shows which pitches are hardest to hear.
options: Patients press a button to stop the test early.
Hearing tests are painful for most patients.
Audiologists wear the headphones during every test.
A hearing test shows which sounds a patient hears.
quests.correctAnswer: A hearing test shows which sounds a patient hears.
quests.hint: For a process, ask what the steps are meant to produce.
quests.explanation: Sounds, button presses and a chart together show what the patient can hear. The button press alone is one step, and 'painful' contradicts the first sentence.
keyPoints: A hearing test is simple and painless.
Patients press a button whenever they hear a quiet sound.
A chart shows which pitches are hardest to hear.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Compost forms when kitchen scraps and dry leaves are piled together. Tiny organisms break the material down, and turning the pile lets air reach them. After several months, the pile becomes dark, crumbly soil that gardeners can add to their beds.
options: Gardeners turn compost piles to keep them warm.
Small organisms break scraps down into soil for gardens.
Dry leaves are more useful than kitchen scraps in gardens.
Kitchen scraps become soil within a few days.
quests.correctAnswer: Small organisms break scraps down into soil for gardens.
quests.hint: Find what does the work in the process and what it produces.
quests.explanation: The explanation says organisms decompose waste into soil, with air helping. Wrong options give a different reason for turning, shorten the timing, or compare materials without support.
keyPoints: Kitchen scraps and dry leaves are piled together.
Organisms decompose them, and turning the pile gives them air.
After months, the result is soil that gardeners can use.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Mobile banking apps confirm every large payment with a text code. The bank sends the code to the registered phone, and the customer types it into the app before the payment goes through. This means that someone who steals a password still cannot take money without the phone.
options: Passwords are no longer needed for mobile banking.
Customers must type a long code for every payment.
Text codes add a second layer of security.
Banks send codes to any phone that asks for them.
quests.correctAnswer: Text codes add a second layer of security.
quests.hint: Ask why the step exists, not only what happens in it.
quests.explanation: The code adds protection because a thief would need the phone as well as the password. The wrong options contradict or exaggerate the process.
keyPoints: Large mobile payments need a text code to be approved.
The code goes to the customer's registered phone.
A stolen password alone cannot move money.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: If you are moving to a new flat, photograph every room before you unpack. Note existing marks, damaged walls and broken handles, and email the photos to the landlord the same day. If a dispute arises about the deposit, this record can protect you.
options: Disputes about deposits are rare when people unpack quickly.
Landlords should photograph rooms before tenants arrive.
Photograph a new flat's condition early to protect your deposit.
Emailing photos is the only way to get a deposit back.
quests.correctAnswer: Photograph a new flat's condition early to protect your deposit.
quests.hint: Recommendation paragraphs usually end with the reason. Use it.
quests.explanation: The writer advises taking photos before unpacking so there is proof if the deposit is questioned. The wrong options change who acts, invent a link with speed or use 'only'.
keyPoints: Photograph every room before unpacking in a new flat.
Record marks, damage and broken items, then email the landlord.
The photos can protect your deposit in a dispute.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Job seekers should tailor each application, even if it takes longer. Read the advertisement carefully and mention the specific skills the employer asks for. Recruiters say they can tell when a letter has been copied, and those applications rarely reach an interview.
options: Interviews are offered only to people who write long letters.
Sending many applications quickly is the best strategy.
Recruiters usually copy letters from other applicants.
Tailoring each job application to the advertisement improves your chances.
quests.correctAnswer: Tailoring each job application to the advertisement improves your chances.
quests.hint: Find both the advice and the evidence the writer offers for it.
quests.explanation: The advice is supported by recruiters' ability to spot copied letters. Wrong options reverse who does the copying, recommend the opposite or exaggerate the requirement.
keyPoints: Job seekers should adapt every application.
They should read the advertisement and mention the skills requested.
Recruiters notice copied letters and rarely invite those applicants.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Parents who want children to read more should let them choose their own books. Comics, magazines and sports biographies all count. Libraries report that children who pick their own titles borrow more, and enjoyment, not difficulty, tends to keep them going.
options: Children should read only comics and magazines at home.
Letting children choose books encourages more reading.
Libraries should choose books on behalf of children.
Difficult books keep children reading for the longest time.
quests.correctAnswer: Letting children choose books encourages more reading.
quests.hint: Find the advice and check that you have not turned a suggestion into a rule.
quests.explanation: The advice is to give children choice, backed by borrowing figures and the role of enjoyment. Wrong options narrow the choice, reverse who decides or contradict the last sentence.
keyPoints: Parents should let children choose their own books.
Comics, magazines and biographies count as reading.
Children who choose borrow more, driven by enjoyment.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The bakery's oven broke on the busiest morning of the year. Instead of closing, the owner borrowed ovens from two nearby restaurants and asked staff to bake in shifts. Customers waited a little longer, but no orders were cancelled.
options: A bakery kept serving customers by borrowing other ovens.
The bakery closed for the day because of the broken oven.
Customers were upset because their orders were cancelled.
Two restaurants now bake bread for the bakery every morning.
quests.correctAnswer: A bakery kept serving customers by borrowing other ovens.
quests.hint: A challenge story has a problem and a response. Which option has both?
quests.explanation: The oven failure was the problem, borrowing ovens was the response, and the orders were still served. Wrong options reverse the outcome or make a temporary help permanent.
keyPoints: The bakery's oven broke on a very busy morning.
The owner borrowed restaurant ovens and used shifts.
Customers waited slightly longer, but no orders were cancelled.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A landslide blocked the only road to Zoltan's mountain village. Residents cleared a narrow footpath by hand, and a helicopter delivered medicine and food. Engineers say the road will reopen in a month, so the village is organising shared meals in the meantime.
options: Engineers have moved the village to a safer place.
Villagers coped with a blocked road using shared work.
The road was reopened after residents cleared it by hand.
Helicopters have replaced the village road for good.
quests.correctAnswer: Villagers coped with a blocked road using shared work.
quests.hint: Check the time words: what is already done, and what is still to come?
quests.explanation: The village dealt with a temporary emergency using footpaths, helicopter supplies and shared meals, while the road waits for repair. The wrong options change the timeline or make temporary help permanent.
keyPoints: A landslide cut off the only road to the village.
Residents built a footpath and a helicopter brought supplies.
The road will reopen in a month, and meals are shared meanwhile.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Naledi was nervous about her first university lecture in a large hall. She arrived early, sat near the front and wrote down one question. When the lecturer invited questions, she asked hers, and several classmates thanked her afterwards for raising it.
options: Naledi sat at the back and stayed silent.
Large lecture halls make almost every student feel nervous.
Classmates thanked Naledi for arriving early to the lecture.
Naledi calmed her nerves by preparing a question.
quests.correctAnswer: Naledi calmed her nerves by preparing a question.
quests.hint: Trace how Naledi's actions respond to her worry.
quests.explanation: Her nerves led to a plan, and following it led to a good result. The wrong options reverse her actions, generalise to all students or misattribute the thanks.
keyPoints: Naledi felt nervous before her first big lecture.
She arrived early, sat near the front and prepared a question.
She asked it, and classmates thanked her.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Ilse's village school was expected to close because only twenty children remained. Parents responded by offering free after-school clubs run by volunteers, from woodwork to chess. Families in neighbouring villages noticed and began to enrol their children. Enrolment has since passed forty, and the closure plans have been withdrawn.
options: Neighbouring villages have closed their own schools.
Twenty children attend the school's woodwork club.
Volunteer clubs helped save a village school.
The school stayed open because the government paid for it.
quests.correctAnswer: Volunteer clubs helped save a village school.
quests.hint: Join the threat, the response and the outcome into a single idea.
quests.explanation: Falling numbers threatened the school, parents' clubs attracted new pupils, and the closure was cancelled. Wrong options misuse a number, invent an event or credit a different rescue.
keyPoints: Ilse's school faced closure with only twenty pupils.
Parents ran free after-school clubs staffed by volunteers.
Enrolment doubled, and the closure plans were withdrawn.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Gustavo's family restaurant used to throw away vegetable peelings and stale bread. Now the cook makes stock from the peelings and turns the bread into soups and puddings. The change cut the food bill by a fifth, and customers like seeing local, thrifty dishes on the menu.
options: Stock is the most expensive item on the restaurant's menu.
Using leftovers in new dishes has cut the restaurant's costs.
The restaurant throws away only stale bread these days.
Gustavo's customers dislike thrifty dishes on the menu.
quests.correctAnswer: Using leftovers in new dishes has cut the restaurant's costs.
quests.hint: Which option shows the change in practice and its benefit?
quests.explanation: Leftovers that used to be waste are now ingredients, which saves money and pleases customers. The wrong options contradict the customers' reaction or misstate what is still thrown away.
keyPoints: The restaurant used to discard peelings and stale bread.
It now turns them into stock, soups and puddings.
Food costs fell by a fifth, and customers like the dishes.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The city library's quiet floor was getting crowded, so noisy group study spilled into the reading area. Staff created a bookable meeting room and put up simple signs asking for quiet talk elsewhere. Complaints dropped, and the meeting room is now full every afternoon.
options: Signs are the only tool libraries need to keep readers quiet.
The quiet floor has been closed to all visitors.
Complaints dropped because staff stopped answering them.
A bookable room gave the library's noisy groups their own space.
quests.correctAnswer: A bookable room gave the library's noisy groups their own space.
quests.hint: Match the problem to the solution that directly answers it.
quests.explanation: Noise was the problem, and a separate space for groups solved it. Wrong options give an extreme fix, a false reason for the drop in complaints or claim signs alone work.
keyPoints: Group study was making the library's quiet floor noisy.
Staff added a bookable meeting room and asked for quiet elsewhere.
Complaints dropped and the new room is used every afternoon.
